results.input: The self-attention mechanism allows each token in a sequence to weigh the relevance of every other token when computing its own representation, rather than relying solely on fixed-size context windows as earlier recurrent architectures did. In practice, this is implemented through three learned projections—queries, keys, and values—whose dot products, scaled by the square root of the key dimension, are passed through a softmax function to produce attention weights. Stacking multiple attention heads in parallel lets the model attend to different types of relationships simultaneously, such as syntactic dependencies in one head and long-range semantic associations in another. This design choice, combined with residual connections and layer normalization, is what allows transformer-based models to scale to billions of parameters without suffering from the vanishing gradient problems that plagued earlier deep recurrent networks. However, the quadratic cost of self-attention with respect to sequence length remains a significant bottleneck for processing very long documents.
results.output: El mecanismo de autoatención permite que cada token en una secuencia peso la relevancia de cada otro token al calcular su propia representación, en lugar de depender únicamente de ventanas de contexto de tamaño fijo como lo hacían las arquitecturas recurrentes anteriores. En la práctica, esto se implementa a través de tres proyecciones aprendidas: consultas, claves y valores, cuyos productos punto, escalados por la raíz cuadrada de la dimensión de la clave, se pasan a través de una función softmax para producir pesos de atención. Apilar múltiples cabezas de atención en paralelo permite al modelo atender diferentes tipos de relaciones simultáneamente, como dependencias sintácticas en una cabeza y asociaciones semánticas de largo alcance en otra. Esta elección de diseño, combinada con conexiones residuales y normalización de capas, es lo que permite a los modelos basados en transformadores escalar a miles de millones de parámetros sin sufrir los problemas de gradiente desvanecido que plagaron a las redes recurrentes profundas anteriores. Sin embargo, el costo cuadrático de la autoatención con respecto a la longitud de la secuencia sigue siendo un cuello de botella significativo para procesar documentos muy largos.

results.input: Reinforcement learning from human feedback has become the dominant approach for aligning large language models with human preferences after pretraining. The process typically unfolds in three stages: first, human annotators rank multiple model outputs for the same prompt according to helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness; second, these rankings are used to train a separate reward model that learns to predict which responses humans would prefer; and third, the original language model is fine-tuned using reinforcement learning, most commonly proximal policy optimization, to maximize the reward model's score. Critics of this pipeline point out that reward models can be gamed through a phenomenon known as reward hacking, where the policy learns to exploit quirks of the reward model rather than genuinely improving response quality. More recent alternatives, such as direct preference optimization, attempt to sidestep the need for a separate reward model entirely by reformulating the alignment objective as a classification problem over preference pairs, which simplifies the training pipeline considerably.

Los críticos de este proceso señalan que los modelos de recompensa pueden ser manipulados a través de un fenómeno conocido como hacking de recompensa, donde la política aprende a explotar peculiaridades del modelo de recompensa en lugar de mejorar genuinamente la calidad de las respuestas. results.input: Empirical scaling laws suggest that a model's loss on held-out data decreases predictably as a power-law function of three factors: the number of parameters, the size of the training dataset, and the amount of compute used, measured in floating-point operations (FLOPs). On standard benchmarks such as MMLU and HumanEval, this approach has closed much of the gap between models an order of magnitude apart in parameter count, though performance on tasks requiring genuine multi-step reasoning still correlates more strongly with scale than with training-token density alone.

results.input: The self-attention mechanism allows each token in a sequence to weigh the relevance of every other token when computing its own representation, rather than relying solely on fixed-size context windows as earlier recurrent architectures did. In practice, this is implemented through three learned projections—queries, keys, and values—whose dot products, scaled by the square root of the key dimension, are passed through a softmax function to produce attention weights. Stacking multiple attention heads in parallel lets the model attend to different types of relationships simultaneously, such as syntactic dependencies in one head and long-range semantic associations in another. This design choice, combined with residual connections and layer normalization, is what allows transformer-based models to scale to billions of parameters without suffering from the vanishing gradient problems that plagued earlier deep recurrent networks. However, the quadratic cost of self-attention with respect to sequence length remains a significant bottleneck for processing very long documents.

En la práctica, esto se implementa a través de tres proyecciones aprendidas: consultas, claves y valores, cuyos productos punto, escalados por la raíz cuadrada de la dimensión de la clave, son pasados a través de una función softmax para producir pesos de atención. results.input: Reinforcement learning from human feedback has become the dominant approach for aligning large language models with human preferences after pretraining. The process typically unfolds in three stages: first, human annotators rank multiple model outputs for the same prompt according to helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness; second, these rankings are used to train a separate reward model that learns to predict which responses humans would prefer; and third, the original language model is fine-tuned using reinforcement learning, most commonly proximal policy optimization, to maximize the reward model's score. Critics of this pipeline point out that reward models can be gamed through a phenomenon known as reward hacking, where the policy learns to exploit quirks of the reward model rather than genuinely improving response quality. More recent alternatives, such as direct preference optimization, attempt to sidestep the need for a separate reward model entirely by reformulating the alignment objective as a classification problem over preference pairs, which simplifies the training pipeline considerably.
results.output: El aprendizaje por refuerzo a partir de la retroalimentación humana se ha convertido en el enfoque dominante para alinear grandes modelos de lenguaje con las preferencias humanas después del preentrenamiento. El proceso se desarrolla típicamente en tres etapas: primero, anotadores humanos clasifican múltiples salidas del modelo para el mismo aviso de acuerdo a su utilidad, honestidad e inocuidad; segundo, estas clasificaciones se utilizan para entrenar un modelo de recompensa separado que aprende a predecir qué respuestas preferirían los humanos; y tercero, el modelo de lenguaje original se ajusta utilizando el aprendizaje por refuerzo, comúnmente mediante optimización de políticas proximal, para maximizar la puntuación del modelo de recompensa. Los críticos de este proceso señalan que los modelos de recompensa pueden ser manipulados a través de un fenómeno conocido como hacking de recompensa, donde la política aprende a explotar peculiaridades del modelo de recompensa en lugar de mejorar genuinamente la calidad de las respuestas. Alternativas más recientes, como la optimización directa de preferencias, intentan eludir la necesidad de un modelo de recompensa separado totalizando el objetivo de alineación como un problema de clasificación sobre pares de preferencias, lo que simplifica considerablemente el proceso de entrenamiento.
